channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan's President outlines 7 national programs for economic and social development
item.description: President outlined seven national programs aimed at national resurgence over the next decade. These cover knowledge, health, technology, water, law, community development, and foreign policy. Key goals include attracting $450 billion in foreign investment, reaching $300 billion GDP by 2030, and creating 2 million high-paying jobs.

item.title: Uzbekistan participates in SCO anti-monopoly meeting in Dushanbe, discusses competition policy
item.description: Uzbekistan's Committee for Development of Competition and Consumer Protection attended a meeting of SCO anti-monopoly bodies in Dushanbe. Discussions focused on international cooperation in competition protection and exchanging practical experience. Uzbekistan reported a decrease in state-owned enterprises' share in GDP and measures taken to curb anti-competitive actions.

item.title: Tashkent housing fraud: Izmir Art Stroy head arrested, new company to continue construction
item.description: The head of Izmir Art Stroy LLC in Tashkent has been arrested as part of a fraud investigation. The company is accused of taking 287 billion soms from 1530 citizens for apartments that were never built. A new company will continue the construction projects.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Russia Sign Cooperation Program to Combat Corruption
item.description: Uzbekistan and Russia have approved a cooperation program to combat corruption for 2027-2028. The agreement, signed by Russia's Prosecutor General Alexander Gutsan and Uzbekistan's Anti-Corruption Agency Director Akmal Burkhanov, includes exchanging experience, implementing digital tools, and developing anti-corruption culture. Both sides aim for more regular and practical bilateral interaction.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan Discuss Migration Issues
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ambassador to Kazakhstan, Kudaybergen Bazarbaev, met with Kazakhstan's Foreign Minister Mukhtar Tileuberdi to discuss bilateral cooperation and migration. The officials reviewed tasks set by the heads of state to elevate relations to a new level of alliance and good neighborliness. They also addressed creating favorable conditions for citizens' stay, transit, and labor activities.

item.title: Uzbekistan Launches Projects Worth $7.5 Billion in Karakalpakstan
item.description: During his visit to Karakalpakstan, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev launched 11 projects valued at $592 million and initiated 47 projects worth $7 billion with foreign partners. These initiatives are expected to create 8,000 jobs. Projects included wind farms, a hospital, a medical academy, a computing center, and public transport upgrades.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Japanese Companies Discuss New Investment Projects
item.description: Uzbekistan's Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov met with Keidanren Chairman Takeshi Hashimoto and leading Japanese companies to discuss economic cooperation. Discussions focused on expanding interaction, creating favorable conditions for foreign firms, and implementing new investment projects in energy, transport, infrastructure, and other sectors.

item.title: Italy to Deploy Warships to Bab al-Mandab Strait to Ensure Safe Passage
item.description: Italy will deploy warships to the Bab al-Mandab Strait to ensure the safe passage of commercial vessels. The move aims to prevent disruptions to global and European economies that could arise if the strategic waterway is blocked, particularly by Houthi forces.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Azerbaijan Sign Energy Cooperation Roadmap
item.description: Uzbekistan and Azerbaijan have signed a roadmap to expand energy cooperation for 2026-2028. The agreement, signed in Baku by energy ministers Sherzod Khodjayev and Parviz Shahbazov, focuses on implementing a green energy corridor, developing oil and gas exploration, and increasing oil product supplies. SOCAR's expansion in Uzbekistan is also a priority.

item.title: Uzbek President Inspects Nukus Insulation Group's Modern European Equipment
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited the Nukus Insulation Group enterprise, which features modern European equipment valued at $50 million. The facility produces goods meeting international standards using local raw materials.

item.title: Qoraqalpogʻiston Launches $7.6 Billion Projects, Starts New Power Capacity Construction
item.description: Qoraqalpogʻiston has launched projects worth $7.6 billion and initiated the construction of new power capacities. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev attended the ceremony, which is expected to create 8,000 high-paying jobs.

item.title: Samarkand to Host World Summit on Child Well-being
item.description: Samarkand will host the World Summit 'Investing in Child Well-being: Towards Sustainable and Equitable Development for Future Generations' on October 21-22. The forum will gather leaders, ministers, international organization representatives, and experts from over 100 countries. Children and adolescents will also participate.

item.title: Favorable Business Environment Fuels Large Projects in Kegeyli
item.description: A favorable business environment is driving major projects in Kegeyli, Karakalpakstan. The 'Kegeyli baraka naslli parranda' poultry enterprise, costing $7.8 million, has created 70 jobs and can house up to 200,000 chickens, producing 27.5 million eggs annually. It also features an automated feed production plant.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Statehood History Discussed Amid Independence Day Celebrations
item.description: Uzbekistan celebrated its 35th Independence Day with a program highlighting the nation's statehood history. Experts discussed political and historical signals, with one noting the emphasis might be linked to activities within the Organization of Turkic States and the importance of self-awareness in the current geopolitical climate.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Agriculture Showcases Test Version of IDyikan Farmer App
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Water Resources, Agriculture, and Processing Industry presented a test version of the IDyikan application for farmers. This platform aims to simplify farmer-state interactions by consolidating digital agricultural services, including animal registration and loan applications, with plans to digitize more services like irrigation water access.

item.title: Central Asia-Korea Summit Adopts Seoul Declaration, Agrees on Biennial Meetings
item.description: The first Central Asia-Korea Summit in Seoul adopted the Seoul Declaration, agreeing to hold presidential-level meetings every two years. Discussions focused on cooperation in supply chains, critical minerals processing, energy, transport, and digital technologies. The second summit is planned for Kazakhstan in 2028.

item.title: Shavkat Mirziyoyev visits Karakalpakstan Academy of Medical Sciences
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited the Karakalpakstan Scientific and Practical Academy of Medicine. The academy can train 3,000 doctors and 6,800 mid-level medical and pharmaceutical staff annually. It will also prepare about 100 clinical residents from the Aral Sea region each year.

item.title: Industrial orchards adapted to local climate expand in Aral Sea region
item.description: Industrial orchards adapted to the local climate are expanding in the Aral Sea region. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited an intensive orchard in Kegeyli district, Karakalpakstan, developed by 'ADM Agro'. The project, costing 55 billion soms, aims to prove the economic viability of horticulture in the region's saline soils.

item.title: Uzbekistan Expands Safe Labor Migration Opportunities Abroad
item.description: Uzbekistan's Migration Agency is expanding safe labor migration routes, coordinating with foreign employers and informing citizens about secure employment abroad. Efforts focus on identifying skilled workers and matching them with vacancies in Germany, the UK, South Korea, Japan, Russia, and other countries. New destinations include Japan and Saudi Arabia.

item.title: Terrorist attack on Karachi mosque during Friday prayers kills 14, injures over 200
item.description: A terrorist attack occurred in a Shia mosque in Karachi during Friday prayers, resulting in 14 deaths and over 200 injuries. The explosion damaged the mosque's walls and windows. Investigators suspect a suicide bomber, supported by eyewitness accounts of an unidentified man present before the blast. The incident led to riots in Karachi.

item.title: Former Kyrgyzstan Emergency Situations Minister Detained for Abuse of Office
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's military prosecutor's office identified violations during the construction of a service building near the Baitik meteorological station. The former Minister of Emergency Situations, identified as A.B., was detained for abuse of office, causing significant state damage. Construction occurred in a prohibited water protection zone.

item.title: Moscow Hotel Manager Sentenced to Three Years for Housing Crocus Attack Convicts
item.description: A Moscow hotel manager has been sentenced to three years in prison for providing accommodation to two individuals convicted in the Crocus attack. The court delivered the verdict, resulting in the manager's imprisonment.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Parliament Speaker and CEC Head Confirm Sadyr Japarov Can Run for President Without Resigning
item.description: Parliament Speaker Marlen Mamataliev and Central Election Commission head Tynychtyk Shainazarov stated that Sadyr Japarov will not resign to participate in presidential elections. They confirmed that a rule allowing a sitting president to run for re-election was introduced long before his term.

item.title: Preventing Domestic Violence and Protecting Women's Rights is a Priority Task
item.description: A meeting in Shakhrinkhan district, Andijan region, focused on preventing domestic violence and protecting women's rights. Measures to support women, ensure their rights, and combat human trafficking were discussed. Emphasis was placed on supporting women with restraining orders.

item.title: Direct Flights to Launch Between Kulob, Tajikistan and Kazan, Russia
item.description: Direct flights will commence between Kulob, Tajikistan, and Kazan, Tatarstan (Russia), operated by Nordwind Airlines starting September 27. Flights will operate weekly, with tickets priced between 1600 and 2500 somoni one-way. The flights will use a Boeing 737-800 aircraft.

item.title: Kazakhstan Days of Medicine in Kyrgyzstan: 1,300 People Examined, Memoranda Signed
item.description: The Days of Kazakh Medicine in Kyrgyzstan concluded with 1,300 people examined and several memoranda signed. Leading specialists from both countries held joint operations, consultations, and master classes. Mobile medical complexes provided services in the Chuy region, examining 1,300 residents.

item.title: Dushanbe Hosts SCO Meeting on Competition Policy Among Member States
item.description: Antimonopoly authorities from Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) member states convened in Dushanbe to discuss competition policy. Tajik officials highlighted the importance of fair competition and adapting policies to the digital economy. The meeting aimed to foster professional dialogue and experience exchange.

item.title: UN Report: Achieving Gender Equality Will Take Over 170 Years
item.description: A new UN report indicates that achieving gender equality at current rates will take 171 years. By 2030, none of the Sustainable Development Goal 5 targets will be met if progress doesn't accelerate. Issues include discrimination, violence, and unequal participation in politics and economics.

item.title: Dushanbe to Host Asian Parliamentary Assembly Standing Committee Meeting
item.description: Dushanbe will host the next meeting of the Standing Committee on Social and Cultural Affairs of the Asian Parliamentary Assembly from September 24-27, 2026. The event, led by Tajikistan, will be the first APA meeting held in the country and aims to foster cooperation and promote sustainable development.

item.title: "Uzbekfilm" to Become Hub for Uzbekistan's Modern Film Industry
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva visited "Uzbekfilm" studio, emphasizing its transformation into a national brand and a hub for the modern film industry. The state's role will shift to a strategic partner, focusing on creating conditions and providing financial support, while private studios and producers will take the lead.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Japan discuss cooperation in training, employment, and investment
item.description: Uzbekistan's Foreign Minister met with the president of 'Onodera User Run' in Tokyo to discuss supporting employment projects for Uzbek citizens in Japan. They also explored creating new educational centers in Uzbekistan and expanding vocational training for youth. Uzbekistan and Japan aim to enhance cooperation in human capital development, employment, and investment.

item.title: Tajikistan discusses specialist training domestically and abroad
item.description: A meeting on specialist training in Tajikistan was held at the Ministry of Education and Science. Deputy Prime Minister Dilrabo Mansuri emphasized the importance of qualified personnel for socio-economic development. Discussions covered coordination, selection mechanisms for overseas study, priority training areas, and aligning specialties with national economic needs.

item.title: Migrant arrivals in Europe decrease, but sea route fatalities rise
item.description: The International Organization for Migration reported a 39 percent drop in migrant arrivals to Europe by sea. However, the number of deaths and disappearances on these routes has increased, with over 2,300 recorded so far this year. The central Mediterranean route saw the sharpest decline in arrivals but a rise in fatalities.

item.title: European Commission proposes banning social media for children under 13
item.description: The European Commission proposed the EU Kids Act to enhance online child safety, suggesting a ban on social media for children under 13. Those aged 13-15 could use 'mini-accounts' with parental controls. The act also imposes obligations on online services to prevent addictive features and limit screen time.

item.title: Tajikistan's Finance Minister discusses new financing mechanisms with Rothschild & Co
item.description: Tajikistan's Finance Minister met with a representative from Rothschild & Co in London to discuss cooperation on issuing government bonds and utilizing new financing mechanisms for priority projects. The meeting also focused on improving Tajikistan's international credit ratings and exploring prospects for bilateral cooperation.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Offer 30% Tuition Discount for Children of Educators
item.description: Starting from the 2026/2027 academic year, Uzbekistan will provide a 30% discount on tuition fees for children of educators enrolled in state higher education institutions. This applies to full-time undergraduate programs. The discount is not applicable to military, foreign, non-state institutions, or joint programs. Applications will be processed via the kontrakt.edu.uz system.

item.title: Tajikistan Responds to ICC on Failure to Arrest Vladimir Putin
item.description: The Tajik government has responded to the International Criminal Court (ICC) regarding its failure to arrest Russian President Vladimir Putin during his visit to Tajikistan. The response details the reasons behind Tajikistan's decision not to detain Putin, despite the ICC's request.

item.title: Migrant Arrivals in Europe Decrease by 39%, While Fatalities Rise
item.description: The number of migrants arriving in Europe by sea has fallen by 39% this year, according to the International Organization for Migration (IOM). Despite the decrease in arrivals, the number of deaths and disappearances at sea has increased. The Central Mediterranean route to Italy saw a 55% drop in arrivals but a rise in fatalities.

item.title: Tajikistan's Pamir petroglyphs and historical sites added to UNESCO tentative list
item.description: Five complexes of petroglyphs in Tajikistan's Gorno-Badakhshan region and four historical-natural sites in Khatlon region have been included in UNESCO's tentative list. The Agency for Protection of Historical and Cultural Heritage stated these sites are valuable examples of Tajikistan's heritage with scientific, cultural, and historical significance.

item.title: UN mission finds US responsible for war crimes in Iran, Tehran for crimes against humanity
item.description: A UN mission found sufficient grounds to believe the US was behind two military strikes on an Iranian school and sports complex, deeming them war crimes. The mission also concluded Iran's government committed crimes against humanity during its violent crackdown on protests.
